subject: Private telemetry adapter mapping & SOC integration plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-fin.com>, secops@acme-fin.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private telemetry adapter mapping & SOC integration plan

Hi Maria / Acme SecOps team,

Thanks for taking time to chat last week. As discussed, we're putting together a concise plan for how Redwood will export telemetry (logs, metrics, traces) from a Private deployment in your VPC to your SIEM and trace collectors with minimal network footprint and without sending sensitive payloads outside your environment.

High-level asks from our side so we can produce an adapter mapping and a PoC runbook:
- A short list of available ingestion endpoints (Splunk HEC, Sumo HTTP, SFTP drop, or SIEM collector IPs) and allowed egress ports.
- Example log samples (redacted) for inference audit logs + access logs + agent health metrics.
- Any mandatory headers or tokens your SIEM requires for ingestion.
- Expected retention and indexing rules that might affect field mapping (PII redaction needs).

We're planning to deliver:
1) adapter_mapping_v1.xlsx — field-level mapping (Redwood log field -> Acme index/field).
2) poc_runbook_v1.pdf — step-by-step to run a short PoC in your staging VPC (collector configs, firewall rules, verification checks).
3) a 2-hour PoC session (we propose Wed 5/19) where our infra engineer will pair with your SecOps for live verification.

Can you confirm the egress constraints and whether a private peering or NAT egress is preferred? Also let us know if you need us to sign an IAM/SC contract before we share unredacted samples.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: adapter_mapping_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 86KB)]

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-fin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@acme-fin.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private telemetry adapter mapping & SOC integration plan

Ben — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers below and attaching a sample of our ingestion spec.

- Ingestion endpoints: Splunk HEC (https://splunk-acme-ingest.acme-fin.com:8088), our on-prem Splunk receiver at 10.10.32.12:8088 (private only), and a secure SFTP drop for batched exports.
- Egress: We prefer private peering to avoid internet egress where possible. If peering not available, NAT egress through our perimeter is allowed on ports 443 and 8088 to specific FQDNs.
- Tokens/headers: HEC requires X-Splunk-Token header; we will provide a scoped token for the PoC.
- Retention/Payload rules: Audit logs with user identifiers must be redacted at write-time unless explicitly permitted (we can provide a redaction whitelist).

Attaching: acme_ingest_spec_v2.pdf and a zip of two redacted sample events (sample_inference_logs_redacted.zip). We cannot share unredacted logs until our legal team signs the NDA; pls confirm if Redwood needs an additional DPA addendum.

We like the proposed 2-hour PoC window. Wed 5/19 works on our side 10:00-12:00 PT. Please send calendar invite.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
Principal SecOps Engineer | Acme Financial
maria.gomez@acme-fin.com
[Attachment: acme_ingest_spec_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 42KB)]

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private telemetry adapter mapping & SOC integration plan

Thanks Maria — and thanks for the sample spec. Attached is adapter_mapping_v1.xlsx (first pass) that maps Redwood's internal log/trace/metric fields to Splunk index fields and flags fields that should be redacted by default. A few notes inline:  

- We default to prefixing inference audit fields with "rw_infer_" to keep them separate from application logs. If you prefer a different namespace we can swap.
- For private peering: our runtime supports routing telemetry over an internal interface; we'll coordinate IPs during the PoC.
- For SFTP: we propose batched export for aggregated metrics and health checks only; not raw traces.
- Tracing: we will send trace sampling headers and a minimal span envelope (no payload content) to your trace collector; full spans remain in your VPC unless you opt-in.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Acme provides scoped HEC token + confirmation of peering window.
2) Redwood shares final PoC runbook (poc_runbook_v1.pdf) and a checklist of firewall rules.
3) Run PoC on Wed 5/19 10:00-12:00 PT.

I've added JIRA ticket OBS-1247 for the work and linked the drive doc: https://redwood.app/drive/1a2b3c-adapter-mapping. Please confirm the token delivery method (DocuSign secure share / vault entry / direct SecOps email).

Great — thanks everyone. Confirming the PoC slot Wed 5/19 10:00-12:00 PT and that we'll bring:
- Ben (infra pairing) + Lauren (adapter mapping owner) + Evelyn (security & redaction checklist)
- Deliverables we will upload before the call: adapter_mapping_v1.xlsx and poc_runbook_v1.pdf (both attached here).

Action items for Acme before PoC:
- Provide scoped HEC token via secure vault or encrypted email to secops@redwood.ai@redwood.ai (we prefer vault entry).
- Confirm whether peering will be available during the window or whether we should prepare NAT-path configs.

I'll open OBS-1247 and include the runbook and a short verification checklist (verify HEC ingest, verify redaction rules, verify sample trace envelope). If there are any network ACL constraints we should know about please flag them in the HubSpot thread.

Looking forward to it — we will run the PoC in staging and not ship any production data.
